segments.text: Chipmaker unveils a laptop processor with all-day battery life. Also coming up: Startup launches satellite internet service for farms. And later, our number of the day. This is TECH BYTES. I'm Max Circuit, with Ada Volt.
From Circuit Weekly: A chipmaker has unveiled a new laptop processor it says can run for 20 hours on a single charge.
segments.headline: Chipmaker unveils laptop processor with all-day battery life

segments.text: And when does it reach actual people?
The first laptops using it will go on sale in the spring.
Circuit Weekly reports that a startup has launched a satellite internet service designed for farms in remote areas. It says the service reaches speeds of 100 megabits per second.
segments.headline: Startup launches satellite internet service for farms

segments.text: Our number of the day: about 1,500 dollars. From Circuit Weekly: A home robotics company has shown a robot vacuum that can climb stairs using two small legs. It will cost about 1,500 dollars when it launches next year.
segments.headline: Robot vacuum learns to climb stairs

segments.text: And finally: Astronomers using a telescope in Chile have detected water vapour in the atmosphere of a planet 120 light years away, Starfield Journal reports. The planet is about twice the size of Earth.
segments.headline: Telescope in Chile spots water vapour on a distant planet

segments.text: Somewhere, a researcher is very pleased with themselves. Rightly.
That's TECH BYTES. From Ada Volt and from me, thanks for watching. More news around the clock on GLOBIT 24.
